text: The student completes the Handbook eligibility checklist.
The title, abstract and keywords also feed the examiner suggestions later.
The softbound date must be at least 3 months away, or the notice is refused.
Once the date is fixed, the notice is filed…
…and the progress tracker starts.
The supervisor endorses it first, or returns it with a comment.
The AE verifies every item.
The notice only passes when all are met.
For another student, Nur Farah, the system reads the Turnitin report itself: similarity, single sources above 5%, title and word count.
Anything that doesn't match is a warning for the AE, never a silent pass.
The AE approves, and the softbound thesis is verified.
Only Available examiners can be picked. Anyone in their 90-day gap is greyed out.
Suggestions are ranked by TF-IDF, and each one shows why it matched.
Conflicts of interest are flagged with the evidence: here, a paper co-written with the supervisor.
An examiner already on another department's list is flagged too.
The supervisor submits the four-seat panel.
Pool states are worked out from dates, so nobody updates a spreadsheet any more.
The AE compiles nominations for the DAC. Nothing reaches CGS without a DAC record.
The compiled list is generated as a PDF for the DAC meeting.
At faculty level, the same examiner nominated by two departments is flagged, not rejected.
Near-identical names are caught too, so one person isn't booked twice.
A viva can only be set once the softbound is verified and the nomination is released.
Lee Jia Hui is ready. Her examiners' report categories differ, so the AE sees it before setting the date.
Weekends, public holidays and clashes are warned about, and the AE decides.
Setting the date sends calendar invites to the student, supervisor, examiners and chair.
Students follow their progress but never see examiner names.
Every re-viva has a formal submission time, so each deadline is calculated from it.
The risk score lists its factors. It's rule-based, not a prediction.
Correction letters and re-evaluation forms are generated automatically.
The Dean approves the pack…
…and CGS sends it to the panel in one click, with signed, expiring links.
The panel gets a working-day deadline: 20 days for Master, 30 for PhD, with reminders before it's due.
